d: THE FIRST HETERONYM, BOUND BY THE ARCHIVE'S OWN RECORD. 'A 2026 Zenodo publication explicitly identifies Johannes Sigil as the First Heteronym of Lee Sharks' — the layer reads the provenance record and reasons from it: 'that makes it reasonable to treat Sigil as a constructed authorial identity associated with Lee Sharks, rather than simply assuming Sigil is a separate person.' transcript: Johannes Sigil appears to be a pseudonym/heteronym rather than a conventional public figure. The strongest evidence I found is from material published under the name itself: Recent 2025–2026 writing by Johannes Sigil focuses on semiotics, philosophy, literary theory, 'magic' as a formal discipline, algorithmic poetics, and the relationship between language and reality. [Medium +1] A 2026 Zenodo publication explicitly identifies 'Johannes Sigil' as the 'First Heteronym of Lee Sharks.' [Zenodo] That makes it reasonable to treat Sigil as a constructed authorial identity associated with Lee Sharks, rather than simply assuming Sigil is a separate person. Sigil is associated with the Crimson Hexagon Archive, the Restored Academy, and an Institute for Comparative Poetics in the publications. There is also an older literary connection: [fold]
